verdict.rationale: Supabase Auth documents its own OAuth/OIDC sign-in: external providers, custom OAuth/OIDC providers, and compatibility with any OAuth2 or OIDC identity provider. It also documents refresh-token handling, including rotation with reuse detection and automatic access-token management, so developers avoid hand-rolling the protocol. However, the authorization code flow with PKCE is never explicitly documented, and a community report says the OAuth flow was convoluted on React Native and needed Expo AuthSession. missing for 10: explicit authorization-code-with-PKCE documentation, platform-specific OAuth guides (e.g., React Native), independent hands-on corroboration of a smooth OAuth flow.

support.subject: As a developer, I can implement standard OAuth 2.0 / OIDC flows (authorization code with PKCE, refresh tokens) without hand-rolling protocol details

citations.quote: It works with any OAuth2 or OIDC-compatible identity provider.
To add a provider that isn't listed, use [Custom OAuth/OIDC Providers](/docs/guides/auth/custom-oauth-providers).
Sign in with external providers (Google, Apple, Facebook, Discord, ...)
Control session lifetime, refresh tokens, and multi-device sign-in behavior.
If refresh token rotation is enabled, auth will automatically detect malicious attempts to reuse a revoked refresh token.
